title: THE ABANDONED VEHICLE
subtitle: Training simulation 03
summary: A confined space with broken glass, upholstery fibres, and one item that no bag can hold safely. Read each description before you choose.
objective: Collect every item. One of them gives off fumes, and this scene carries a container you have not used before.

background.alt: The inside of a car seen from the back seat, with two front seats, a steering wheel, a dashboard, a shattered side window, and a wet floor mat

evidence.name: Fuel-soaked rag
evidence.alt: A crumpled cloth with a dark wet patch and rising fumes
evidence.description: A cloth in the passenger footwell, heavy with petrol. You can smell it from the doorway.
evidence.success: The airtight can holds the petrol vapour in, so the lab can still identify which fuel was used.
evidence.failure: Petrol vapour passed straight through this packaging. Within days there was nothing left to identify.

evidence.name: Glass fragment
evidence.alt: An angular fragment of window glass
evidence.description: A sharp fragment from the shattered side window, resting on the dashboard.
evidence.success: The rigid container holds the sharp edge still, protecting both the fracture pattern and the handler.
evidence.failure: The fragment cut its way out, endangering whoever carried it and losing the fracture edge.

evidence.name: Screwdriver
evidence.alt: A screwdriver with a red handle
evidence.description: A screwdriver pushed under the driver's seat. The tip is scratched and burred.
evidence.success: Held rigid, the tool cannot rub against anything, so its tip marks stay comparable.
evidence.failure: The tip rubbed against its packaging and the tool marks that could match it to a break-in were worn away.

evidence.name: Upholstery fibre
evidence.description: A single red fibre on the passenger seat, a different colour to this car's upholstery.
evidence.success: Sealed and visible, the fibre stays where it was put and can still be matched to a source.
evidence.failure: The fibre worked its way out of the packaging and can no longer be tied to this vehicle.

evidence.name: Wallet
evidence.description: A dry wallet in the footwell behind the driver's seat, cards still inside.
evidence.success: The wallet and everything inside it stay together and sealed away from the rest of the scene.
evidence.failure: The wallet was not sealed, so its contents and any prints on them were exposed in transit.

evidence.name: SIM card
evidence.description: A dry SIM card tucked into the driver's door pocket.
evidence.success: The sealed bag stops this very small item from disappearing into a corner of the box.
evidence.failure: Something this small slipped out of its packaging and never reached the laboratory.

evidence.name: Blood swab
evidence.alt: A cotton swab with a red-stained tip
evidence.description: A swab taken from a smear on the driver's seat. The tip is still wet.
evidence.success: The wet swab dries in the breathable packaging, keeping the blood sample fit for DNA analysis.
evidence.failure: Sealed while wet, the swab grew bacteria and the DNA in the sample broke down.

evidence.name: Drink can
evidence.description: A half-full can in the cup holder. The rim is damp and may carry saliva.
evidence.success: The damp rim dries out instead of stewing, so the saliva on it is still worth testing.
evidence.failure: The liquid left inside kept the rim wet and the saliva sample spoiled before it was tested.
